classification.difficultyReason: Use similar triangles to express the upper parallel side in terms of the height, then substitute into the trapezium area formula.

content.prompt:
An isosceles triangle has base 16 cm and height 12 cm.

An isosceles trapezium is inscribed with its longer parallel side along the base of the triangle.

The trapezium has height $x$ cm. Show that the area of the trapezium is $A=16x-\dfrac{2x^2}{3}$.

spec.description: Unlabelled upright isosceles triangle with a horizontal segment between its sloping sides, forming the upper boundary of the inscribed trapezium. Schematic proportions carry no additional measurements.
spec.mathematics: The trapezium shares the triangle's full base; its other parallel side joins the two sloping sides.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete unlabelled diagram remains visible in the student edition.

sizing.reason: Restore the source-calibrated full figure height and width; preserve all drawing coordinates, camera, extrusion and native label font size.

answer.short: By similar triangles, the upper parallel side is $\dfrac{16(12-x)}{12}=16-\dfrac{4x}{3}$ cm. Hence $A=\dfrac12\left(16+16-\dfrac{4x}{3}\right)x=16x-\dfrac{2x^2}{3}$ cm².
answer.worked:
By similar triangles, at height $x$ cm above the base, the width of the triangle is $\dfrac{16(12-x)}{12}$ cm.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Top of trapezium}&=\frac{16(12-x)}{12}\\\text{Top of trapezium}&=16-\frac{4x}{3}\end{align*}$$

Bottom of trapezium $=16$ cm.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12(\text{top}+\text{bottom})\times\text{height}\\A&=\frac12\left(16-\frac{4x}{3}+16\right)x\\A&=16x-\frac{2x^2}{3}\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
